subject: Renewal health + capacity bridge: proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Mike O'Neill <mike@codexlabs.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: anjali@codexlabs.com
Date: 2025-05-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Quick: renewal health review before exec sync

Camila —

We're prepping for our exec decision on June 15 and need a short readout from Redwood on our Q1–Q2 consumption and performance. High level asks: monthly token spend trend, any latency regressions by model, and a short ROI note tying cost to reduced human review time (we track saved FTEs).

We saw a spike during the April pilot (roughly +40% month-over-month). We're evaluating a 2x committed capacity for the next 12 months if the numbers justify it. Can Ben or you share an economic bridge and proposal we can take to procurement?

Attachments: Codex_Q1_usage_summary.csv (exports of token counts by model)

Thanks —
Mike
CFO, Codex Labs
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Mike O'Neill <mike@codexlabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-23T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: renewal health review before exec sync

Mike —

Thanks for the context and the CSV. We've pulled preliminary numbers: average token spend March–May increased from 1.1M to 1.54M tokens/month, driven by two burst windows tied to your nightly batch rerank and the new summarization flow. Latency for the primary model (redwood-qa-large) remained within SLO (p50 120ms, p95 420ms) but we observed p99 spikes during bursts — attached is the latency dashboard screenshot.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Ben: draft a 12-month committed-capacity proposal with a 2x tier and burst lane (no change to pricing model, with a 12% volume discount at that commit level).
- Marissa: coordinate a short ROI paragraph documenting 0.6 FTEs saved in customer ops per month from the summarization rollout.
- Camila (me): compile a 1-page executive summary and a procurement-ready DocuSign attachment.

I'll circulate a concise package by EOD Monday. Would you prefer the proposal to include a short SLA credit for sustained p99 > 700ms?

Best,
Camila
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, Mike O'Neill <mike@codexlabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-26T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: renewal health review before exec sync

Adding the economics: Mike, attaching a short bridge file in the Drive link (see related links) and summarizing here:
- Current run-rate: ~$16.8k/month (token-only) based on 1.54M tokens/mo.
- Proposed 2x commit tier: committed spend ~$36k/month with 12% discount (effective unit price drop ~10–12%) + 200k burst credits per month at no surcharge for 90-day ramp window.
- Estimated token cost reduction: ~28% on marginal unit economics after commit.
- Latency SLA addendum: we can include a p99 credit structure (credit = 5% monthly credit if p99 > 700ms for more than 3 days in the month).

I'll prepare a redlined term sheet and DocuSign packet. Camila — want me to include a one-time 30% onboarding credit for your burst in April? That would accelerate approval but impacts the effective first-quarter ARR.

—Ben
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Mike O'Neill <mike@codexlabs.com>
Date: 2025-06-03T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: renewal health review before exec sync

Mike —

Couple of ROI items to include in the exec packet:
- Baseline: manual review required ~3.8 FTE-hours/day before summarization; after rollout it's ~1.6 FTE-hours/day (Codex reported), so ~0.6 FTE decrease equivalent when averaged across the month given load variability.
- Estimated annualized labor savings at $85k fully loaded: ~$33k for the current production load; at 2x capacity that's ~66k (we'll model conservative adoption at 70% of total capacity).
- Other benefits: reduced time-to-insight (~35% faster incident triage) and fewer escalations (tracked as 18% reduction in late-stage tickets).

I've added the ROI paragraph to the executive summary and dropped a short contact at Procurement for a rapid signature pathway.

Attachments referenced: renewal-bridge-proposal-DocuSign.pdf

Cheers,
Marissa
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Mike O'Neill <mike@codexlabs.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-10T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: renewal health review before exec sync

Camila / Ben / Marissa —

This package looks solid. A couple of quick asks before the 6/15 exec:
1) Can we get the final DocuSign with the 2x commit + 30% onboarding credit included? Procurement prefers a single-signature flow.
2) Please add the SLA p99 credit language as Ben suggested.
3) One-sheeter for exec: 1 paragraph on usage trend, 1 paragraph on ROI (with the $ figures), and the term summary.

If you can send the DocuSign and one-sheeter by EOD Wednesday (6/11), I'll route to Procurement and Legal immediately. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Thanks —
Mike
CFO, Codex Labs
